exposure: Women with a single episode of preeclampsia followed by normotensive pregnancies
Women who developed severe preeclampsia in subsequent pregnancies
Women who developed mild preeclampsia in subsequent pregnancies
cohort: 213,558 multiparous patients with a singleton gestation who delivered at Soroka University Medical Center (Beer Sheva, Israel) from January 1988 until December 2012
finding: Recurrent preeclampsia was associated with an increased rate of pregnancy complications in subsequent pregnancies compared to a single episode of preeclampsia.
birth_weight: Neonates born to mothers with recurrent preeclampsia had lower mean birthweight compared to those with a single episode.
